root_cause.text: The AMD display debugfs handler `dp_sdp_message_debugfs_write()` in `amdgpu_dm_debugfs.c` assumed `connector->base.state->crtc` was always valid and used a fixed-length user copy instead of the actual write size, leading to a NULL dereference on unbound connectors and a buffer over-read from `copy_from_user()`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (!connector->base.state || !connector->base.state->crtc) return -ENODEV;` before `to_dm_crtc_state(connector->base.state->crtc->state);`, and introduces `write_size = min_t(size_t, size, sizeof(data));` after the CVE/commit message states the function "dereferences connector->base.state->crtc without checking for NULL" and "always passes 36 bytes to copy_from_user(), reading past the user buffer when size < 36."

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the debugfs SDP message write path by validating connector/CRTC state before use and bounding the copied user data size.
intent_record.what: The change adds an early check that returns -ENODEV if connector->base.state or connector->base.state->crtc is missing, and it moves/introduces initialization of write_size using min_t(size_t, size, sizeof(data)) before copy_from_user().
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents dereferencing a missing connector state or CRTC when handling the debugfs write path, avoiding invalid access or crashes, and ensures copy_from_user() uses a bounded, initialized write length based on the input size and local buffer capacity.

grouping_result.intent: Fix the debugfs SDP message write path by validating connector/CRTC state before use and bounding the copied user data size.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly match the root cause: they add connector/CRTC state validation to avoid NULL dereference and limit copied user data to the actual write size instead of a fixed length, addressing the buffer over-read.

candidates.rationale: This directly dereferences connector->base.state->crtc without validating that the connector is bound to a CRTC, causing the NULL pointer dereference described in the root cause.
This performs the user copy using write_size rather than the actual user-supplied size bounds, matching the root cause that a fixed-length copy could over-read user data.

This relies on the prior copy_from_user length handling and reflects the flawed fixed-size copy logic; if the copy length was wrong, the resulting write_size accounting is also based on unsafe assumptions.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement dereferences connector->base.state->crtc->state without first verifying that the connector is currently bound to a CRTC, which directly causes the NULL dereference described in the root cause.
This copies a fixed write_size from userspace instead of limiting the copy to the actual user-supplied write length, causing the buffer over-read condition described in the root cause.

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit c7ba3653e9773256b2b08508a2ed2ca28ea7566b
Author: Leo (Hanghong) Ma <hanghong.ma@amd.com>
Date:   Thu Mar 7 16:18:12 2019 -0500

    drm/amd/display: Generic SDP message access in amdgpu
    
    [Why]
    We need to add DP SDP message test debugfs to make sdp message test
    more convenient and efficient.
    
    [How]
    Add sdp_message debugfs entry in amdgpu.
    
    Signed-off-by: Leo (Hanghong) Ma <hanghong.ma@amd.com>
    Reviewed-by: Sun peng Li <Sunpeng.Li@amd.com>
    Acked-b
bic_trace_step.reason: The function body is sufficient to determine the issue because it directly shows both relevant behaviors. First, it dereferences `connector->base.state->crtc` without checking whether `connector->base.state` or `connector->base.state->crtc` is NULL: `acrtc_state = to_dm_crtc_state(connector->base.state->crtc->state);`. This matches the NULL-dereference root cause for unbound connectors. Second, it uses a fixed copy length regardless of the actual user write size: `uint32_t write_size = 36;` followed by `r = copy_from_user(data, buf, write_size);`. There is no validation that `size >= 36`, so if userspace writes fewer than 36 bytes, the kernel still attempts to copy 36 bytes from the user buffer, matching the described fixed-length copy bug. The code does not contain the fix: there is no guard for a missing CRTC/state, and no use of the actual `size` to bound the copy.
